body.note: Game values: the size is the commonly quoted one but was not in the research extracts.

drive.note: Engine 225 kW (UTD-20, 300 hp) and road speed 65 km/h are published; reverse speed, gear bands, efficiency, braking, steering, idle power and fuel use are game values.

ramp.note: Game value (M7), not in the public sources; tuned in the drive lab. Two rear doors.

stations.note: Traverse 360 deg in 10.28 s, elevation -5 to +74 deg through 74 deg in 12.33 s, two-plane stabiliser 2E36-1 (published); errors and tolerance are game values. M7.3: 2A42 with both belts ready (160 AP, 340 HE: the published 500) and the PKT (250 ready, 7 belts stowed: the published 2000); owner Q17: ready belts refilled from stowage in battle, halted, about 90 s. Owner 2026-11-13 ("Yes, add the ATGM"): the 9P135M launcher on the turret roof with one 9M113M missile on it (three more stowed: four in all, published); the gunner guides it (SACLOS) and puts the next one on in 40 s, halted. Balance pass 5 (F9, low; search extracts: Battlefront forum on the BPK-2-42, weaponsandwarfare.com and redstar.gr on the BPK-3-42, Frag Out! magazine on the TKN-3B): the gunner's BPK-2-42 night channel (image intensifier, IR searchlight) sees to about 850 m (vehicle-night-gen1; it was vehicle-night-ir, 3000 m); the commander's TKN-3B gets its night channel, below about 400 m (vehicle-night-short). Balance pass 5 review (C21, low): the 9M113M is guided through the 9Sh119M1 sight beside the launcher, a day sight (plan balance-5 C21, search extracts), so `guideSensors` [vehicle-day]: no Konkurs guidance through the BPK-2-42 night channel.

vehicles.note: BMP-2: 3 crew (commander and gunner in the turret, driver in the hull) and 7 passengers (FAS). Swimming is not modelled. Armour, components and signature come with M7.3/M7.4. M7.2: stowed rifle magazines and machine-gun belts for the squad (game values, low): the men refill from a halted vehicle. M7.3: 2A42 and PKT, smoke dischargers, seat sights (commander day, gunner day and night). The driver (buttoned up, owner Q5) drives and does not search for the enemy (game value). M11.1: also cans of loose rounds for the squad (1 x ru-545-tin, 1 x ru-762r-tin): what is really carried is not sourced (low).

dischargers.note: 902V Tucha, six 81 mm launchers (published); range, delay and cloud are game values.

armour.note: Rolled steel armour (resistance 1.25 = RHA). Search extracts give the BMP-1/2 hull as welded steel of about 7-19 mm on the front (upper glacis 7 mm at 80 degrees, lower 19 mm at 57 degrees), 16-18 mm sides, 16 mm rear, the turret up to 23 mm, protection against 12.7 mm from the front and small arms elsewhere; one plate per part and face here: hull front 18 mm at 60 degrees (45 mm mild steel along a level path), sides 18 mm (22.5), rear 16, roof 7, turret front 23 mm at 35 degrees, sides 16 at 20, rear 15, roof 7. Effect: the front stops 23 mm AP at 500 m, the sides stop 7.62 mm AP but not 12.7 mm; every cannon round and rocket in the game penetrates.

components.note: Game values. The fuel tanks in the hollow rear doors and between the troop seats, and the ready ammunition in the turret basket, are as commonly described (search extracts); boxes, toughness and chances are game values. M7.4b: transmission, turret drive, stabiliser, coaxial MG, sights, radio, smoke dischargers and extinguisher added (where they commonly sit; boxes and toughness are game values).

extinguisher.note: Game values: the BMP-2 carries a fire-extinguishing system (search extracts); its charges, delay and chance are not published. Lower than the Puma's: fuel in the rear doors and between the seats (owner: the BMP-2 burns easily).

repair.note: M11.7a field repair: the kit the crew needs and the parts each crew task uses up (game values from forum and test-drive search extracts, research 2026-11-16, low).

body.note: BTR-80 hull: 7.65 x 2.90 m (search extracts); the BMM has no turret, so the height is the hull roof (game value about 2.35 m). Hull box and effective steering wheelbase are game values.

mass.note: Combat weight 13.6 t (one source gives 12.6 t; search extracts only).

drive.note: BTR-80: KamAZ-7403 diesel of 260 hp (191 kW) and 80 km/h on roads are published (search extracts). Five gear bands (manual gearbox, slower shifts), reverse speed, braking, steering (about 25 m turning circle), idle power and fuel use are game values (low). Swimming is not modelled.

ramp.note: Game values: the BTR-80's side doors between the second and third axles; a stretcher through a side door is slow.

signature.note: Game values: a low hull without a turret; quieter than the tracked carriers.

armour.note: Search extracts give the BTR-80 welded steel of about 10 mm on the front and 7-9 mm on the sides, rear and roof: proof against rifle fire and fragments, not heavy machine guns. One plate per face.

components.note: The BTR-80 has its engine at the rear and the crew at the front (search extracts); boxes, toughness and chances are game values; 'wheels': each side's running gear (a wrecked side immobilises it).

ambulance.note: BMM (BMM-1 'Simfoniya' family on the BTR-80): crew of three; up to 9 patients, 7 in the medical compartment and 2 on stretchers outside on the hull, or 4 stretchers inside plus 2 outside (search extracts; a third source says 4 in all). Unarmed apart from the crew's rifles; marked with the red cross.

vehicles.note: BMM armoured medical vehicle on the BTR-80 (M10.6-data): the first Russian wheeled vehicle. Crew of three: driver, commander and a medic (seat 'med', a crew seat of the generic kind 'loader': no weapon uses it, and he can take over the driving); seats p1-p7 are the sitting places inside. No weapon station (the BTR-80 turret is removed). Ambulance behaviour comes with M10.6a.

repair.note: M11.7a field repair: the kit the crew needs and the parts each crew task uses up (game values from forum and test-drive search extracts, research 2026-11-16, low).

body.note: 9.63 x 3.78 x 2.2 m with the gun forward (ArmsNet; War Thunder 9.6 x 3.8 x 2.2): the hull 6.9 m long (not found: game value from the T-72 family), the gun 4.58 m past the turret front; boxes, clearance and track figures are game values.

mass.note: 46.5-48 t in the sources (wardatalab 46.5, Army Recognition about 48): 48 t used (low).

drive.note: V-92S2F, 1130 hp (843 kW) and 60 km/h (published, medium; 60-70 in some sources). Reverse: one gear, 4.8 km/h (the T-90 family's slow reverse, from memory, low). Gear bands, efficiency, braking, idle power and fuel use are game values (low). A turn on one track is modelled as a slow pivot at 20 deg/s (game value).

ramp.note: Game values (M7.6a): no ramp; the crew gets in and out through the hatches (bailing out of the low, cramped turret slower than from a Leopard).

stations.note: Two-plane stabilised turret with the Kalina fire control and Sosna-U thermal sight with laser rangefinder (published, medium). The carousel's 22 rounds (ready: 12 3BM60, 9 3OF26 and one 9M119M, game split); 10 3BM60, 8 3OF26 and 3 missiles more in the hull and bustle (43 in all). The autoloader takes 7 s a round (published 7 s / about 7 a minute in combat, low); a round is in the breech at the start. The missile is fired through the gun (separate weapon entry: its own count), chosen against vehicles beyond 2500 m (game value). Traverse, elevation 10 deg/s, -6 to +14 degrees, errors and tolerance are game values. Refilling the carousel from the hull racks, halted: 240 s (game value).

dischargers.note: 902B 81 mm smoke launchers, twelve (published for the T-90M; not found for the T-72B3M): two salvos of six. Range, delay and cloud are game values as the BMP-2's.

armour.note: Game values from public estimates only (armour is classified; FAIR's 1100-1200 KE / 1900 CE with Relikt is taken as optimistic): line-of-sight equivalents at 0 degrees, one plate per face, with Relikt tiles as counted items. Base without tiles: turret front about 550 mm RHA against long rods / 650 against jets (550 mm cast-with-filler: 687 / 814 mm mild steel), hull front 480 mm (600 / 710), turret side 200 mm (250 / 296), hull side 80 mm steel, rear 40 / 70 mm, roof 20 / 40 mm. Relikt coverage of a hit and tiles fitted per face (turret front 0.85 of 26, turret side 0.5 of 10, hull front 0.75 of 20, hull side 0.6 of 12) are game values (counts not public; Janes notes a line of seven on the lower glacis). Not modelled: slat and net screens, roof cages (M14.5), a weaker lower glacis or mantlet.

components.note: Game values: the carousel under the turret (a penetration often blows it up: cook-off 0.45), more rounds in the bustle (behind a partition: 0.1) and in the hull racks beside the driver (0.5); fuel front right; engine and transmission at the rear.

extinguisher.note: Game values: automatic fire suppression (charges, delay and chance are not published).

signature.note: Game values: a low hull and turret (size 0.95); type known within 2 km.

vehicles.note: T-90M Proryv main battle tank (M7.6a): 3 crew (driver front centre, gunner turret left, commander turret right), carousel autoloader. Search extracts only (pages not opened in this container). Published (medium): engine, speed, crew, 22-round carousel, 43 rounds in all (40 in another source), Sosna-U and PK-PAN thermal sights, Relikt, 2A46M-5, Refleks-M. Game values (low): armour, tiles, components, stowage split, reload 7 s, signature. Laser warner (low: a Shtora-type warning set reported).

mass.note: 45-47 t in the sources: 46 t used (low).

drive.note: V-92S2F, 1130 hp (843 kW) and 60 km/h (published, medium; some T-72B3 pages 70). Reverse: one gear, 4.2 km/h (from memory, low). Other drive values as the T-90M's (game values).

stations.note: Two-plane stabilised turret with Sosna-U (thermal, laser rangefinder, published; one source says 1PN96MT-02 on the B3 family). The carousel's 22 rounds (ready: 12 3BM60, 9 3OF26 and one 9M119M, game split); 8 3BM60, 7 3OF26 and 3 missiles more (40 in all, low). Balance pass 5 (F10, low; search extracts: Army Recognition T-72B3M data sheet, weaponsystems.net T-72B3, the 125 mm ammunition and 2A46 reference pages): the B3's 2A46M-5 comes with a modified autoloader that takes the long Svinets rods (3BM59 / 3BM60), so the carousel round is the 3BM60 as on the T-90M (it was the 3BM42 Mango of the old carousel; one forum post disagrees). The autoloader takes 7.5 s a round (low: 'likely about 8 s'); a round is in the breech at the start. The commander has a day sight only. Other values as the T-90M's (game values).

dischargers.note: 902B 81 mm smoke launchers, twelve (published for the T-90M; not found for the T-72B3M): two salvos of six. Range, delay and cloud are game values as the BMP-2's.

armour.note: Game values from public estimates only: line-of-sight equivalents at 0 degrees, one plate per face. Base without tiles: turret front about 430 mm RHA against long rods (published T-72B estimates about 410 KE / 500 CE: 430 mm cast-with-filler, 537 / 636 mm mild steel), hull front 420 mm (525 / 622), turret side 180 mm (225 / 266), hull side 80 mm steel, rear 40 / 60 mm, roof 20 / 40 mm. Tiles (Janes, medium for the layout): Kontakt-5 on the turret (front 0.85 of 26, side 0.5 of 6), Relikt on the upper glacis (0.75 of 18) and the side skirts (0.6 of 12); Relikt on the turret front only from the 2025 model. Coverage and counts are game values.

components.note: Game values: the carousel under the turret (cook-off 0.45) and the loose rounds in the hull (0.6, no bustle rack); fuel front right; engine and transmission at the rear.

signature.note: Game values: a low hull and turret (size 0.95); type known within 2 km.

vehicles.note: T-72B3M (T-72B3 obr. 2016) main battle tank (M7.6a): 3 crew, carousel autoloader. Search extracts only (pages not opened in this container). Published (medium): engine, speed, crew, 22-round carousel, Sosna-U, Relikt on the glacis and skirts, Kontakt-5 on the turret. Game values (low): armour, tiles, components, 40 rounds in all (38-45 in the sources), reload 7.5 s, signature. 3BM42 is the carousel round here (low: the B3M's newer autoloader may take 3BM59/60). No laser warner (not found). No turret bustle rack.

repair.note: M11.7a field repair: the kit the crew needs and the parts each crew task uses up (game values from forum and test-drive search extracts, research 2026-11-16, low).

body.note: BTR-82A: 7.65 x 2.90 x 2.80 m (Army Recognition; the state catalogue gives 7.58 x 2.985 x 2.725 m), ground clearance 0.475 m (BTR-80 figures; search extracts). Hull roof about 2.1 m, the turret box and the effective steering wheelbase are game values (low): the wheelbase is the BMM's (same BTR-80 chassis), which with its steering gives a turning circle near the published 13.2 m radius (axles 0 / 1.35 / 3.05 / 4.40 m).

mass.note: Combat weight 15.4 t (most sources; 14.55 t and 16 t also quoted; search extracts).

drive.note: KAMAZ 740.14-300 turbo diesel of 300 hp (221 kW; army-technology) and 80 km/h on roads (Army Recognition, ROE; other sites 90-100); search extracts. Gear bands, reverse speed, braking, steering, idle power and fuel use as the BMM's (same BTR-80 chassis; game values, low). Swimming is not modelled.

ramp.note: Game values: the BTR-80's two side doors between the second and third axles, cramped (dismounting 1.5 times the BMP-2's rear doors' time per man); the roof hatches are not modelled.

stations.note: BPPU-type turret with the 2A72 and the PKTM coax, stabilised in two planes, elevation -5 to +70 degrees (army-technology, army-guide; search extracts, medium). 300 ready 30 mm rounds (medium), split 100 AP / 200 HE (low) and no 30 mm stowed; 2,000 PKT rounds (medium): 250 ready, seven belts stowed, refilled in battle, halted, in about 90 s (as the BMP-2's; low). The gunner's TKN-4GA-02 day / passive-IR sight (later builds: the TKN-4GA-03 thermal imager, not modelled); no laser rangefinder (low). Traverse, elevation rate and errors are game values (low).

vehicles.note: BTR-82A eight-wheeled armoured personnel carrier (M7.6c, slice 41) on the BTR-80 chassis: crew of three (commander, gunner, driver) and seven dismounts (army-technology, ROE, Army Recognition; search extracts only). Balance pass 5 review (low; the same correction as the BMP-2's, plan balance-5 C19): the gunner's TKN-4GA-02 combined sight has an image-intensifier night channel, about 850 m (vehicle-night-gen1), the commander's TKN-3 one below about 400 m (vehicle-night-short); both were vehicle-night-ir, 3000 m, which no source gives. Sources conflict: some batches (and the BTR-82AM / later deliveries) are said to carry a thermal channel; kept an image intensifier until a firmer source, listed in STATE. Infantry stowage as the BMP-2's (game value, low). M7.6d: four SVD magazines stowed for the squad's marksman (game value, low). M11.1: also cans of loose rounds for the squad (1 x ru-545-tin, 1 x ru-762r-tin): what is really carried is not sourced (low).

dischargers.note: 902V Tucha, six 81 mm launchers on the turret (army-technology, search extract, medium); range, delay and cloud are game values as the BMP-2's.

signature.note: Game values: the BMM's hull with a small turret; quieter than the tracked carriers.

armour.note: Search extracts: the front stops 12.7 mm (not 14.5 mm), the sides and rear 7.62 mm; the BTR-80 hull is about 7-9 mm of high-hardness steel (upper front 9 mm at 64 degrees, about 21 mm along the line of sight), the 82A adds a spall liner. Armour-steel equivalents (game values): hull front 10 mm at 64 degrees (28.5 mm mild steel: stops 12.7 mm AP at 500 m), sides 14 mm at 15 degrees and rear 13 mm (the thin hard plate and the spall liner: they stop 7.62 mm AP at 75 m, but not 12.7 mm), roof 7; turret front 20 mm at 30 degrees, sides 10 at 20, rear 8, roof 6. Every cannon round and rocket in the game penetrates.

components.note: Hull parts as the BMM's (BTR-80: engine at the rear, crew at the front); the turret's gun, coax, drive, stabiliser, sights and smoke launchers, and the ready 30 mm belts under the turret (game values, low; 'wheels': each side's running gear).

extinguisher.note: Game values as the BMP-2's and the BMM's.

repair.note: M11.7a field repair: the kit the crew needs and the parts each crew task uses up (game values from forum and test-drive search extracts, research 2026-11-16, low).

A Leopard 2 (64 t) is refused. Tow speed 8 km/h across country (low). Hook-up 240 s by two men outside (tow bar and cables; research 2-5 min with dismounts: game value, low).

vehicles.note: BREM-1 (M11.7b): armoured recovery vehicle on the T-72 chassis (winch 25 t, crane, dozer blade; crew 3: commander, driver, mechanic; search extracts, medium). Unarmed in the game (its machine gun is left out, D11): an off-map asset called from the battalion's repair and evacuation group, outside the side's strength. The BREM-L / BREM-K of the BMP and BTR battalions are later data.

In 2023 military police units received 'Patrul' vehicles for 9-10 men (rg.ru, aif.ru extracts; medium for the vehicle, low for its prisoner role); 10 seats here (driver, commander, eight behind).
